title: Compiler warnings as an engineering feedback system
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: Compiler warnings identify suspicious constructs, conversions, unused values and portability concerns. A project can establish a warning policy, treat selected warnings as errors and review changes when compiler versions introduce new diagnostics.
understand.whyItMatters: Warnings provide fast feedback before runtime tests. A consistent policy improves code quality but should be tailored to the compiler and project context.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.
